planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to deep shade; Shishi Botan is more heavily textured and slightly more sun-tolerant than smooth-leaved leopard plant cultivars but still needs shelter from hot afternoon sun.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to deep shade, sheltering the foliage from hot midday and afternoon sun that can scorch its fuzzy leaf surface. Shishi Botan is a striking Farfugium japonicum selection with heavily crimped, three-dimensional gray-green leaves covered in fine silvery hairs, giving the whole clump an unusual curled, parsley-like texture unlike the flat, glossy leaves of the species. Bright yellow daisy-like flowers rise on tall stalks in fall, providing late-season color above the foliage mound. It spreads slowly into a dense, sculptural clump and makes an eye-catching textural accent in a shaded border or large container.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial shade; ligularia wilts dramatically in dry soil or hot afternoon sun and needs reliable moisture and shade to look its best.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, keeping the root zone from drying out even briefly. Midnight Lady produces large, rounded, glossy purple-black leaves that hold their near-black color more consistently through the growing season than many other dark-leaved ligularia cultivars, which tend to fade toward green as summer progresses. Bold panicles of gold daisy-like flowers with orange overtones rise on dark purple stems in late summer to early fall, contrasting dramatically against the foliage. It is an excellent bold accent for a shaded, moisture-retentive border or pond-edge planting, and divides well every three to four years in spring.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in rich, consistently wet to moist soil, spacing clumps well apart since this cultivar grows considerably taller and more robust than dwarf rocket-type ligularia selections.

directions: Plant in heavy, fertile soil that stays consistently wet to moist, such as a pond margin or low, boggy spot, since this cultivar wilts quickly if the soil dries out even in shade. Morning sun with shelter from hot afternoon sun keeps leaf scorch to a minimum during summer heat. Weihenstephan is a robust, upright selection of rocket ligularia with deep green, heart-shaped, toothed leaves on dark reddish-brown stems, producing narrow, densely packed spikes of small yellow flowers well above the foliage from midsummer into fall. It grows considerably taller than compact rocket ligularia cultivars, making it a dramatic vertical accent for the back of a shaded bog garden or streamside planting.

common_name: Silver Mist Mondo Grass (Variegated Mondo Grass)

planting.note: Plant divisions or plugs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; brighter light than deep shade helps keep the white striping crisp, though foliage still scorches in hot direct sun.

directions: Plant divisions 4 to 8 inches apart in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, watering regularly until the tufts knit together. Silver Mist is a variegated selection of common mondo grass, with narrow, arching, dark green leaves boldly striped in silvery white, giving a brighter, more luminous effect than plain green mondo grass in a shaded planting. Small, pale lavender flowers hide among the foliage in summer, followed by dark blue berries. It slowly spreads by short rhizomes into a dense, fine-textured mat and works well as a shade groundcover, path edging, or container accent where its variegated foliage can be appreciated up close.

planting.note: Plant small divisions or plugs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Gyoku Ryu grows extremely slowly, so set plugs close together if a solid carpet is wanted within a few seasons.

directions: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, keeping the planting evenly watered while the tiny tufts spread together into a mat. Gyoku Ryu is among the smallest mondo grass selections in cultivation, forming a dense, tight carpet of thick, dark green, grass-like foliage that rarely exceeds 2 inches tall, even shorter than standard dwarf mondo. Tiny pale lavender flowers appear on short stalks in summer but are largely hidden within the foliage. Its miniature scale makes it ideal for filling joints between stepping stones and pavers, edging small shade beds, or fairy-garden and miniature landscape plantings where a very low, fine-textured groundcover is needed.

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in rich, well-drained soil in deep shade during spring or early fall; growth is very slow, so choose a permanent, protected spot for this collector's cultivar.

directions: Plant this collector's selection in loose, humus-rich soil in deep shade where little else will thrive, watering regularly the first season while the thick rootstock establishes. Zansetsu, whose name translates to 'remaining snow,' produces tight, upright clumps of dark green leaves heavily streaked and blotched with creamy white variegation, a striking departure from the plain deep-green foliage of the species. Inconspicuous flowers form at the base in fall, followed by short spikes of bright red berries that persist through winter. Growth is exceptionally slow even for a rohdea, so it is best treated as a prized, long-lived specimen for a protected woodland container or shaded rock garden rather than a groundcover.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Fuji No Yuki Rohdea (Snow On Mt. Fuji Sacred Lily)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in rich, well-drained soil in deep shade during spring or early fall; growth is slow, so choose a permanent, protected spot for this variegated collector's cultivar.

directions: Plant in loose, humus-rich, well-drained soil in deep to partial shade, watering regularly the first season while the thick rootstock establishes. Fuji No Yuki ('Snow on Mt. Fuji') produces long, dark green, arching leaves edged in a wide, crisp white margin, creating strong two-tone contrast in a deep-shade planting where variegated foliage is hard to keep both vivid and undamaged by sun. Inconspicuous flowers hidden at the base in fall are followed by short stalks of bright red berries that persist through the winter holiday season. Like other rohdea, growth is slow and maintenance is minimal once established, making it a long-lived specimen for a shaded woodland bed or container.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant divisions or rooted stolons in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; good drainage over winter is important since the cultivar is less rugged than the plain green species.

directions: Plant divisions or rooted stolons in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, working in compost to help retain even moisture. Maroon Beauty forms a low, dense cushion of rounded, scalloped, dark olive-green leaves marked with burgundy-wine coloring and reddish undersides, richer and darker than the plain species. Thin, wiry stems carry loose sprays of small white flowers, some petals etched with purple, above the foliage in mid to late spring, and threadlike red stolons tipped with plantlets spread the clump outward in the same strawberry-like fashion as the species. It is a colorful, low-maintenance choice for a shaded rock garden, woodland edge, or hanging basket where its trailing runners can cascade over the rim.
